text:
maya: hey team, we're hitting a 400 from /v1/tools/execute when using the TS SDK function-calling. server says schema error: 'args' must be an object but is a string. this started after upgrading to ts-sdk@1.2.3. any ideas?

alejandro: sorry to hear that — can you paste a tiny repro and the exact error payload? also which SDK version you upgraded from?

maya: upgraded from 1.2.1 -> 1.2.3. repro below. calling a simple tool 'translate' that expects {text: string}. using client.tool.call. responses: 400 + body: {"error":"invalid_schema","field":"args","message":"expected object"}

```ts
// repro.ts
import Redwood from 'redwood-sdk';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });

await client.tools.call('translate', {
  args: JSON.stringify({ text: 'hola' }) // this is what TS SDK is sending internally in 1.2.3
});
```

maya: curl to our API (raw) with object works fine:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tools/translate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $RW_KEY' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"name":"translate","args":{"text":"hola"}}'
```

alejandro: ok thanks. sounds like the SDK is double-serializing the args for JS. pinging eng-oncall @simon and sdk lead @rachel. can you add logs from the gateway showing request body?

simon: looking. gateway logs show:

POST /v1/tools/translate  400
Request body: {"name":"translate","args":"{\"text\":\"hola\"}"}  <-- args is a string

simon: by contrast, python client sent: {"name":"translate","args":{"text":"hola"}} and succeeded.

rachel: thx for the details. that matches a bug I remember — js serializer was special-casing Objects in call payload and running JSON.stringify on them before sending, because it attempted to support some legacy callers that passed strings. regression landed in 1.2.2 and made it into 1.2.3.

rachel: quick repro I ran locally:

```node
// node repro.js (ts compiled)
const client = new (require('redwood-sdk')).default({ apiKey: 'x' });
client.tools.call('translate', { args: { text: 'hola' } }).catch(e => console.error(e.response?.data || e.message));
// network shows body args:"{\"text\":\"hola\"}" in v1.2.3
```

rachel: workaround for customers right now: explicitly pass a JS object but ensure you are not pre-stringifying. if you're using the higher-level helpers that auto-format, pin to 1.2.1 or use the canary I just pushed.

rachel: pushing a fix to main that removes the extra stringify for args. will open a canary build and ask infra to promote.

tom: ci-bot started canary build job #4827
ci-bot: canary redwood-js@1.2.4-canary.0 pushed, artifacts: https://ci.redwood.ai/builds/4827

rachel: deploying canary to us-west-2 now.
ci-bot: deploy canary -> us-west-2 started (job 4828)

ci-bot: deploy canary -> us-west-2 succeeded (job 4828) — service versions: redwood-gateway:2.14.1-canary, redwood-js:1.2.4-canary.0

rachel: quick patch note: change in src/transport/serializer.ts — removed JSON.stringify on args when payload type === 'tool_call'. also added unit tests to verify nested objects are preserved. commit a1b2c3d4.

simon: gateway logs after canary show incoming body from js sdk still changed? double-checking. network shows correct shape: {"name":"translate","args":{"text":"hola"}}

maya: confirmed on our side. pinned ts-sdk to canary, retried, 200 OK and tool returned translated text. huge thanks. :tada:

alejandro: great — i'll follow up with the customer success ticket and recommend upgrading to 1.2.4 when it's released.

rachel: will cut a patch release 1.2.4 tomorrow with the fix and a short changelog.

maya: thanks everyone, appreciate the fast response. will reopen here if anything else pops up.
